narrativeReportMd:
# DeviceDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `DeviceDefinition` artifact identity but substantially remodels the resource. Hard R4-to-R6 instance breaks are present: R6 adds mandatory `status`, removes or renames several R4 paths, narrows `manufacturer[x]`, changes mandatory `deviceName.type` from primitive code to CodeableConcept, repurposes `version`, and redesigns property values.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions, package metadata, package indexes, and related local terminology resources. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are out of scope unless a local DeviceDefinition element changed its own path or type.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is a shift from an instance-oriented device component description to a canonical, publishable device definition/catalog artifact. R6 adds canonical metadata and lifecycle status, moves type/classification into richer backbones, and adds regulatory, packaging, version, link, guideline, corrective-action, and charge-item structures. Several R4 fields are not simple renames; they require semantic review.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact validation breaks are `status` becoming mandatory; `deviceName.type` changing shape and code system; `property.valueQuantity`/`valueCode` becoming mandatory single `value[x]`; `DeviceDefinition.type` moving to repeatable `classification.type`; and `version` changing from repeatable device/software versions to a single business version. The `url` change is especially risky because old values may still validate while meaning something different.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for status assignment, manufacturer string normalization, name-type code mapping, classification mapping, version classification, capability/conformance mapping, owner/support/publisher separation, URL semantics, parent/packaging/physical-characteristic migration, and preserving R6-only regulatory or safety content in R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes are probably justified by the R6 catalog/canonical model, but several could have been made less disruptive with deprecated aliases, profile-level requirements, or official cross-version extensions. The most avoidable breaks are same-name semantic reuse (`url`, `version`) and mandatory primitive-to-complex representation changes (`deviceName.type`).

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover base artifacts, referenced datatypes, DeviceDefinition search parameters, and official terminology/ConceptMap support for device name types and device classification.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `DeviceDefinition` has hard breaking changes despite retaining the same canonical identity. The top concerns are mandatory `status`, extensive path/type remodeling, and same-name semantic shifts for `url` and `version`. The main uncertainty is the lack of official cross-version ConceptMaps and narrative migration notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a model transformation, not a field rename. First assign canonical metadata and lifecycle status, then convert renamed or remodeled fields (`manufacturer`, `deviceName.type`, `classification`, `deviceVersion`, `property.value[x]`, `outputLanguage`), and finally preserve R6-only or unmatched R4 content through extensions or manual review.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both local StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for semantic equivalence and terminology mapping where official diffs, narrative pages, terminology expansions, and ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: R6 adds mandatory DeviceDefinition.status

oldState.summary: R4 DeviceDefinition had no status element.
oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 `DeviceDefinition` instance could omit lifecycle or publication status entirely because the element did not exist on the resource.

newState.summary: R6 requires status 1..1 code bound to publication-status.
newState.narrativeMd: `DeviceDefinition.status` is mandatory in R6 and must use `draft`, `active`, `retired`, or `unknown` from the required publication-status value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break: a minimal R4 `DeviceDefinition` can be structurally valid with no lifecycle status, while every R6 instance must carry `status`. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy unless `status` is preserved in an extension or side channel because R4 has no local element for it.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: `DeviceDefinition` is being treated more like a publishable definitional artifact, and a lifecycle status supports filtering and safe use. The breakage is material because R4 instances had no such element, but making `status` mandatory in the base resource is probably reasonable for that canonical-resource goal, especially because `unknown` exists for uncertain status.
justification.inferredGoal: Align DeviceDefinition with canonical definitional resources that expose lifecycle metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `status` optional in the base resource and require it only in publication profiles or workflows.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have added `status` as `0..1` and required it through R6 publication profiles, IGs, or repository policy. That would preserve old R4 instances without inventing a status, but it would mean base R6 DeviceDefinitions could still lack the lifecycle state that canonical consumers expect.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Optional base status would preserve R4 instances but weaken uniform lifecycle filtering for a canonical-style R6 resource.

evidence.detail: No R4 element with this id or path exists.
R6 defines `DeviceDefinition.status` as 1..1 code with required publication-status binding.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses `unknown` only as an illustrative fallback. Production migration should select a status according to stewardship policy rather than default silently.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a required lifecycle status on `DeviceDefinition`. This is the clearest hard instance-breaking change because an otherwise valid R4 resource can fail R6 validation solely by omission. The change also signals that R6 treats the resource more like a publishable definition than an instance-oriented description.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation fails when `status` is absent. Strict parsers and generated R6 classes may also require a non-null enum or code. R6-to-R4 conversion loses the lifecycle state unless it is mapped to an extension because R4 has no corresponding element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 DeviceDefinitions without lifecycle metadata, define a status assignment policy, and test migration with missing, known-active, retired, and uncertain artifacts. Do not blindly mark all historical resources `active` if that would affect publication, catalog, or regulatory behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The mandatory element supports a stronger R6 publication model, but it was not the only possible design. Optional base cardinality plus profile-level requirements would have reduced instance breakage while preserving a path for stricter ecosystems.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 makes `DeviceDefinition.status` mandatory where R4 had no such element, so a minimal or otherwise complete R4 instance fails R6 validation until a lifecycle status is assigned. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid break, but the R6 goal is coherent for a definitional artifact because status supports lifecycle filtering, and the `unknown` code gives a non-false assertion path when migration policy cannot determine the status.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no `DeviceDefinition.status`; R6 defines `DeviceDefinition.status` as 1..1 `code` with required `publication-status` binding.
R6 status requirements say it enables tracking the content lifecycle and filtering appropriate DeviceDefinitions.
R4 maturity map lists DeviceDefinition as FMM 0, standards-status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern; without path-specific production evidence for missing status, the hard break alone is not enough for Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances without status become invalid R6 instances, and generated R6 models may require a non-null status.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could add `status` as 0..1 and require it in publication profiles, but that would weaken uniform lifecycle filtering for a canonical-style resource; the required `unknown` option reduces the migration burden.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard break and an optional-status alternative, but its High impact is softened by FMM 0 and by the reasonable lifecycle goal.

findings.title: manufacturer[x] was renamed and narrowed to a Reference-only manufacturer

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 choice serialized as `manufacturerString` or `manufacturerReference`, allowing a plain manufacturer name without an Organization resource.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 element is no longer a choice and expects a Reference-shaped value named `manufacturer`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short text and target profile identify R6 `manufacturer` as the direct successor to R4 `manufacturer[x]`, but the string choice was removed and the JSON property name changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance using `manufacturerString` is invalid in R6 because the primitive choice type was removed. Even R4 instances using `manufacturerReference` need a JSON property rename to `manufacturer`. Generated models also change from a choice accessor to a single Reference property.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing manufacturer data toward an Organization reference is reasonable, but the base R6 break is not clearly necessary. R4 already supported `Reference(Organization)`, and retaining the string branch with deprecation or guidance would preserve text-only catalogs while still allowing structured manufacturer identity.
justification.inferredGoal: Normalize manufacturer identity as an Organization reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `manufacturer[x]` with the R4 string and Reference choices, while clarifying and preferring Organization references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backwards-compatible R6 design could have kept `manufacturer[x]` and marked the string branch as legacy or discouraged, or kept the choice while tightening narrative guidance around legal representative versus actual manufacturer. This avoids invalidating `manufacturerString` and avoids the JSON property rename, at the cost of continued choice-handling and some non-normalized legacy values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost is keeping a choice element and allowing text-only manufacturers longer, but the R6 Reference shape does not guarantee resolvable identity either.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a 0..1 choice of string or Reference(Organization).
R6 defines a non-choice 0..1 Reference(Organization).

examples.examplesMd: A display-only Reference may preserve the label syntactically, but systems that require resolvable Organization references will need Organization creation or matching.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 let implementers record a manufacturer as either free text or an Organization reference. R6 removes the string branch and changes the serialized property name. This breaks both wire-format validation and generated choice-property APIs for systems that populated manufacturer data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: `manufacturerString` is not an R6 element, and `manufacturerReference` is not the R6 property name. A converted R6 instance must carry a Reference object at `manufacturer`. R6 content is mostly representable in R4 by converting `manufacturer` back to `manufacturerReference`, but text-only R4 content requires a policy decision.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `manufacturerReference` to R6 `manufacturer`. For `manufacturerString`, either create or link an Organization, map the string to `manufacturer.display`, or preserve the exact string in an extension if display-only references are not acceptable. Test both choice branches.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The normalization goal could have been achieved less disruptively by retaining the choice and deprecating the string branch. Removing it provides a cleaner R6 shape but creates avoidable migration and codegen churn.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a simple manufacturer string or an Organization reference; R6 only allows `Reference(Organization)`. Manufacturer identity is central to device catalogs and UDI/regulatory contexts, and migrating a plain string may require creating or selecting an Organization resource and deciding whether the value represents a manufacturer, labeler, legal representative, or jurisdictional responsible party.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.manufacturer[x]` is 0..1 `string` or `Reference(Organization)`; R6 `DeviceDefinition.manufacturer` is 0..1 `Reference(Organization)` only.
R6 definition broadens the role to manufacturer or legal representative/labeler depending on implementation and jurisdiction.

HL7 R4 DeviceDefinition scope describes catalog definitions authored by regulatory or local entities; ONC ISP lists the HL7 Cross-Paradigm UDI Pattern Release 2 as Final/Production for UDI representation.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Although DeviceDefinition is FMM 0/trial-use, the affected path is central to the artifact and plausibly used in production device/UDI catalogs, so low FMM does not fully offset the migration risk.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - any R4 `manufacturerString` is invalid in R6, and code generators also lose the choice-type accessors.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A practical less-breaking base design would retain `manufacturer[x]` or add a manufacturer display string while recommending Organization references for computable exchange. The tradeoff is weaker referential computability, but it avoids forcing local identity-management decisions during migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's hard-break finding and Yes alternative are supported; FMM 0 tempers broad impact but not enough to dismiss this central path.

findings.title: deviceName.type changed from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept with a reduced local code system

oldState.summary: R4 used a mandatory primitive code bound required to device-nametype 4.0.1.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local complete R4 CodeSystem contains `udi-label-name`, `user-friendly-name`, `patient-reported-name`, `manufacturer-name`, `model-name`, and `other`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 JSON used a scalar string such as `model-name` in the `type` field of each `deviceName` backbone.

newState.summary: R6 uses mandatory CodeableConcept with extensible device-nametype binding.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local complete R6 CodeSystem contains `registered-name`, `user-friendly-name`, and `patient-reported-name`. The binding is weaker than R4, but the wire type changed from primitive `code` to `CodeableConcept`.

semanticText.comment: The implementation or jurisdiction must clarify which name is to be used as the registered-name.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 expects a `CodeableConcept`; jurisdictional guidance may be needed for the new `registered-name` category.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `deviceName.type` is 1..1 inside every `deviceName`, every R4 deviceName entry uses a primitive string where R6 expects a CodeableConcept object. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy for multi-coding CodeableConcepts and the new `registered-name` code, and old R4 codes need semantic mapping.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of richer, jurisdiction-aware device name typing is reasonable, and the R6 binding is less rigid than R4. The change is still a guaranteed serialization break for every populated R4 `deviceName.type`; however, avoiding that break would require carrying parallel representations or delaying the richer model.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer coding and jurisdiction-specific naming semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 primitive code during transition and add a richer CodeableConcept representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept the R4 `type` code and added an optional CodeableConcept successor, or introduced a transitional paired element. That would cover common R4 instances but would leave implementers with two fields for the same name-type fact and would still require policy for removed R4 codes such as `model-name`, `manufacturer-name`, and `other`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old payloads but create duplicate mandatory name-type representations and ambiguous precedence between primitive and coded forms.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `code`, cardinality 1..1, required binding to device-nametype 4.0.1.
R6 type is `CodeableConcept`, cardinality 1..1, extensible binding to device-nametype.
Local R4 and R6 complete code systems show removed R4 codes and added `registered-name`.

examples.examplesMd: The `model-name` to `registered-name` mapping is illustrative only; some R4 names may be better represented as text or local codings under the extensible R6 binding.

findings.narrativeMd: `deviceName.type` is both structurally and terminologically different. The primitive code becomes a CodeableConcept, and the local HL7 code system no longer contains several R4 codes. This affects validators, generated enum switches, JSON transforms, and user-facing name-type logic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 `deviceName.type` string is not valid R6 JSON for a CodeableConcept. R6 CodeableConcepts can contain multiple codings or text that cannot be reduced safely to one R4 required code. Terminology validation changes are nuanced because R6 weakens the binding to extensible while also changing the core code list.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert primitive R4 codes to CodeableConcept codings and define a ConceptMap-like policy for `udi-label-name`, `manufacturer-name`, `model-name`, and `other`. Include tests for each R4 code, unknown local codings, and R6 `registered-name` round trips.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition could have preserved the R4 primitive code or added a new optional richer element. The selected R6 shape is cleaner but makes every populated R4 `deviceName` require transformation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology comparison used local CodeSystem concepts, not a terminology server expansion. Human review is needed for name-type mapping policy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `deviceName.type` changed from a required primitive code to a required CodeableConcept, and the local complete code system dropped several R4 codes such as `udi-label-name`, `manufacturer-name`, `model-name`, and `other`. Old JSON wire format is invalid in R6, and migration may require semantic judgment about whether the old name category maps to `registered-name`, free text, or a non-core coding.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type` is 1..1 `code` with required `device-nametype|4.0.1` binding; R6 is 1..1 `CodeableConcept` with extensible `device-nametype` binding.
R4 `CodeSystem-device-nametype` contains `udi-label-name`, `manufacturer-name`, `model-name`, and `other`; R6 contains `registered-name`, `user-friendly-name`, and `patient-reported-name`.
Device names are part of catalog/UDI identification; ONC ISP lists UDI representation specifications as production maturity.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 lowers the general compatibility expectation, but this is a central identification field and the code removals can make migration lossy or expert-dependent.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 primitive-code instances fail R6 structure validation, and old codes from the same complete code system may fail terminology validation or require remapping.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have introduced CodeableConcept while retaining the R4 codes as deprecated concepts or a transitional choice/profile path. That would add terminology clutter, but it would preserve old instances and let migration be mechanical for common name types.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the current report correctly sees a high-impact break, but the less-breaking alternative appears stronger than merely partial because deprecated-code retention would meet much of the R6 goal.

findings.title: DeviceDefinition.type was removed and replaced by repeatable classification.type

oldState.summary: R4 had a single optional CodeableConcept `type` with example binding to device-kind.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the kind of device directly at `DeviceDefinition.type`.

newState.summary: R6 uses 0..* `classification` backbones, each with required `classification.type` and optional `justification`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can carry multiple classifications and per-classification justification; the device type value is nested at `classification.type`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short definitions both describe what kind of device this is. R6 adds a repeatable classification wrapper and justification.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing top-level `type` are invalid in R6 because the element path was removed. R6 instances with multiple classifications or justifications cannot be represented losslessly in the single R4 `type` field.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting multiple classifications, risk classes, and justification is a reasonable R6 goal. A top-level `type` cannot express the full R6 structure, so the new backbone is warranted; the main question is whether the R4 field had to be removed immediately.
justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple classifications, risk classes, and evidence for classification.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep top-level `type` as a deprecated primary classification while adding repeatable `classification`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `DeviceDefinition.type` as a deprecated compatibility alias for the primary or first classification while adding `classification.type` for richer use. That would avoid breaking R4 payloads with `type`, but it would introduce synchronization and precedence rules, and deprecated classification representations might accumulate rather than disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alternative preserves old instances but creates duplicate same-resource ways to express device classification, with risk that the deprecated path persists indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `DeviceDefinition.type` as 0..1 CodeableConcept with example device-kind binding.
R6 defines nested required `classification.type` under repeatable `classification` with example device-type binding.

examples.examplesMd: The illustrative R6 `RelatedArtifact` is abbreviated; the point is that justification and multiple classifications have no R4 base slots.

findings.narrativeMd: The device kind/type surface moved from a single top-level CodeableConcept to a repeatable classification backbone. This is a path-level break for R4 payloads and a representability break for R6 payloads that use multiple classifications or justification.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `type` is an unknown element in R6. A simple R4 type can map to `classification[0].type`, but the reverse is lossy if more than one classification is present or if `classification.justification` is populated. Terminology guidance also changes from `device-kind` to `device-type`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `type` to one R6 `classification.type`. If local systems distinguish primary type, risk class, and regulatory class, define ordering or extensions. For R6-to-R4, choose a primary classification or preserve extra classifications in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model is more expressive, but a deprecated top-level `type` could have preserved old instances. The downside would be ambiguity between `type` and `classification.type`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4's single top-level `type` moved to repeatable `classification.type` in R6. This is a real path and API break for populated instances, but the migration is usually direct (`type` becomes one `classification.type`) and the R6 structure better supports multiple classifications, risk classes, national product codes, and justifications.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.type` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with example `device-kind` binding.
R6 `DeviceDefinition.classification` is 0..* and `classification.type` is 1..1 `CodeableConcept` with example `device-type` binding.
R6 classification comment names multiple classification systems including GMDN, EMDN, SNOMED CT, risk classes, and national product codes.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the path-rename concern; the affected field is important, but the R6 design goal and mostly mechanical migration make the break proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances using top-level `type` are invalid against R6 and generated APIs move the property under `classification`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping a deprecated top-level `type` alongside `classification` would preserve old instances, but it would create duplicate representations and consistency questions between the old primary type and the new repeatable classifications.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the report correctly identifies the break and possible legacy field, but High impact is stronger than the path-level evidence warrants under FMM 0.

findings.title: DeviceDefinition.version changed from repeatable device versions to a single canonical business version

oldState.summary: R4 `version` was 0..* string for available device versions.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `DeviceDefinition.version` for available versions of the device, for example software versions.

newState.summary: R6 `version` is 0..1 string for the business version of the DeviceDefinition; device/software versions move to `deviceVersion.value`.

semanticText.definition: The identifier used to identify this version of the DeviceDefinition when it is referenced in a specification.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 repurposes `version` as canonical artifact metadata and adds repeatable `deviceVersion` backbones for device or software versions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with more than one `version` is invalid in R6 because the maximum cardinality is now 1. Even a single R4 value may be semantically wrong if it describes a device software version rather than the business version of the definition.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating the business version of the DeviceDefinition from device or software versions is a reasonable goal, and generic canonical tooling expects the canonical business version at `version`. Reusing the R4 path is risky because a single old value may still validate with the wrong meaning, but the canonical convention makes a fully compatible alternative incomplete.
justification.inferredGoal: Adopt canonical artifact versioning while modeling device or software versions separately.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve repeatable R4 device/software versions and add a separate business-version element for the definition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have left R4 `version` repeatable for device/software versions and introduced a new `definitionVersion` or `businessVersion`. That would avoid invalidating arrays and semantic traps for old data, but it would make DeviceDefinition inconsistent with the standard canonical `url|version` pattern and generic consumers might miss the version.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves R4 data but diverges from the common FHIR canonical-resource convention that uses `url` plus `version`.

evidence.detail: R4 `version` is 0..* string and means available versions of the device.
R6 `version` is 0..1 string and means business version of the DeviceDefinition.
evidence.quote: 0..1 string; Business version of the DeviceDefinition

evidence.detail: R6 adds repeatable `deviceVersion` with mandatory string `value` for device or software versions.

examples.examplesMd: If an R4 value was already a business version for the definition, it may belong in R6 `version`; if it was a device/software version, it belongs in `deviceVersion.value`.

findings.narrativeMd: The same element name survives, but its cardinality and meaning change. That is risky because automated transforms that simply keep `version` may produce R6 resources that validate but mean the wrong thing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Multiple R4 `version` values fail R6 max-cardinality validation. Single values can pass structurally but be semantically misplaced. R6 `deviceVersion.type` and `component` cannot be represented directly in R4 `version` strings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify existing R4 `version` values before transforming. Move device/software version lists to `deviceVersion.value`; reserve R6 `version` for the business version of the DeviceDefinition itself. Add regression tests for multiple versions and single ambiguous versions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The separation is justified but could have been implemented with less reuse of the old path. A profile or deprecation period would have helped consumers distinguish structural compatibility from semantic compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 reuses `DeviceDefinition.version` for the business version of the DeviceDefinition and narrows it to 0..1, while R4 used repeatable `version` for available device or software versions. Multiple R4 versions become invalid, and even a single R4 value can silently change meaning unless a migrator knows whether it is a device/software version or a definition version.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.version` is 0..* string defined as available versions of the device, e.g. software versions.
R6 `DeviceDefinition.version` is 0..1 string defined as the business version of the DeviceDefinition and used with canonical `url|version` references.
R6 adds repeatable `DeviceDefinition.deviceVersion.value` for device or software version text.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 reduces stability pressure, but version data is central to device/software identification and the same-path semantic repurposing can silently mislead systems, so the concern remains material.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances with more than one `version` fail R6 validation; semantic/API break - single values can validate while being interpreted as a different kind of version.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep the repeatable device/software `version` path and add a distinct business-version element, or use a new device-version path without repurposing the old one. The tradeoff is divergence from the common canonical-resource `url`/`version` pattern.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report catches the hard break and partial alternative, but the key issue is the silent semantic repurposing rather than cardinality alone.

findings.title: property values changed from repeatable valueQuantity/valueCode lists to a mandatory single value[x] choice

oldState.summary: R4 property allowed zero or more valueQuantity and zero or more valueCode entries.
oldState.narrativeMd: Each R4 property had required `type` but could have no value, multiple quantities, multiple code values, or both value element families.

newState.summary: R6 property requires exactly one value[x] with a broader choice type set.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a single choice value per property. CodeableConcept values serialize as `valueCodeableConcept`, not the R4 `valueCode` element name.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both models represent property values under `DeviceDefinition.property`, but R6 changes the representation to a FHIR choice element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 properties with no values become invalid because R6 requires one value. R4 properties with arrays or both quantity and code values must be split or normalized. R6 properties using new value types, such as boolean or Attachment, cannot be represented in R4 without extensions.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making each property carry one explicit value and broadening supported datatypes are reasonable R6 goals. The R4 model allowed value-less properties, multiple values, and separate quantity/code lists, so preserving all old instances would undercut the normalized one-value semantics.
justification.inferredGoal: Make each property carry one explicit value while supporting more value datatypes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain legacy repeatable `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` while adding the normalized single `value[x]` choice.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A transitional base design could have kept `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` as deprecated aliases and added new value types. That would cover many R4 payloads, but it would leave ambiguous cases where old and new value fields coexist, and it would not fully enforce the R6 rule that each property has exactly one value.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy aliases would reduce wire breakage but create duplicate property value representations and require invariants for empty, multi-valued, or mixed values.

evidence.detail: R4 `valueQuantity` is 0..* Quantity.
R4 `valueCode` is 0..* CodeableConcept.
R6 `value[x]` is 1..1 with Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, or Attachment.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows one possible split of a multi-valued R4 property into multiple R6 property repetitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The `property` backbone changed from a permissive multi-value pattern to a normalized one-value choice. This is a high-risk codegen and transform area because both the JSON names and collection semantics change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `property` entries with missing values fail R6 validation. R4 `valueCode` arrays are unknown under R6 because the CodeableConcept choice name is `valueCodeableConcept`, and a R4 array must be converted to one or more single-value R6 property entries. R6 new value types are not R4-representable without extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each R4 property, decide whether multiple values should become repeated R6 properties, a combined CodeableConcept, or an extension. Reject or quarantine value-less properties unless a value can be derived. Test all old and new choice-type branches.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is understandable for semantic clarity, but a transition alias or 0..* choice would have avoided some hard instance breaks. The tradeoff is that legacy aliases would complicate validation and downstream processing.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 represented property values as separate repeatable `valueQuantity` and `valueCode` lists, while R6 requires exactly one broader `value[x]` choice per property. Existing instances with zero values or multiple values under one property need restructuring, but the R6 one-property/one-value model is cleaner and supports more value types.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.property.valueQuantity` and `valueCode` are each 0..*.
R6 `DeviceDefinition.property.value[x]` is 1..1 with Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, or Attachment choices.
R6 property definition frames these as static or essentially fixed characteristics, with dynamic properties handled elsewhere.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 and lack of quick path-specific production evidence for multi-valued properties soften the break; the migration burden is real but appears proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 property entries with legacy value names, no value, or multiple values do not directly validate as R6; runtime/API/codegen - generated accessors change to a single choice element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could retain legacy `valueQuantity`/`valueCode` while adding `value[x]`, but that creates duplicate value locations and precedence rules. Splitting multi-valued properties into repeated R6 property entries is a reasonable migration cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the hard serialization break is real, but the existing High impact is softened by FMM 0 and by the improved normalized model.

findings.title: languageCode was replaced by outputLanguage with a primitive required all-languages binding

oldState.summary: R4 `languageCode` was 0..* CodeableConcept with no local binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed coded, text-only, or multi-coding representations for device output languages.

newState.summary: R6 `outputLanguage` is 0..* primitive code with required binding to all-languages.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 expects one primitive language code per repetition using the all-languages value set.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element short text is the same in substance: languages supported for human-readable strings produced by the device.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `languageCode` are invalid in R6 because the path was removed and the representation changed from CodeableConcept to primitive code. Some CodeableConcepts can map cleanly to language codes, but text-only or multi-coding concepts may not.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing supported output languages to standard language codes is reasonable, but the supplied evidence does not show that the R4 path and CodeableConcept shape had to be removed to accomplish that. CodeableConcept can carry standard language codes, and stricter expectations could have been introduced through binding guidance or profiles.
justification.inferredGoal: Normalize output languages to standard language codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `languageCode` as a repeatable CodeableConcept and clarify that standard language-code codings are preferred or expected.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design could have retained `DeviceDefinition.languageCode` with clearer definition and a preferred or extensible all-languages binding, or added `outputLanguage` while keeping the old path as deprecated. This would preserve R4 coded and text-bearing values, though it would not give the same simple primitive-code array or strict base validation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alternative keeps a more flexible representation and weaker base validation, but it avoids a path rename and primitive/complex type break for a rare optional field.

evidence.detail: R4 defines 0..* CodeableConcept.
R6 defines 0..* code with required all-languages binding.

examples.examplesMd: Text-only CodeableConcepts need manual normalization to language codes.

findings.narrativeMd: The supported-output-language field was renamed and simplified. This is a normalizing change, but it is hard-breaking for any R4 instance that populated `languageCode`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: `languageCode` is unknown in R6, and a CodeableConcept object is not valid where R6 expects primitive `code` repetitions. R6 values can often be represented in R4 as CodeableConcept codings, but that conversion is not native and may require choosing a coding system.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Extract language codes from R4 CodeableConcept codings where possible. For text-only values, map manually to valid all-languages codes or preserve the original text in an extension. Include tests for multiple languages and local/nonstandard codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model is more interoperable for language matching, but keeping a deprecated CodeableConcept path would have reduced breakage for existing catalogs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `languageCode` and R6 `outputLanguage` describe the same concept, but R6 changes the path from CodeableConcept to primitive code with a required all-languages binding. Populated R4 instances need a wire-format and terminology migration, but standard language tags should map mechanically in most cases and the element is peripheral to the core device catalog.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.languageCode` is 0..* CodeableConcept with no local binding.
R6 `DeviceDefinition.outputLanguage` is 0..* code with required `all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4` binding.
Both R4 and R6 definitions describe language codes for human-readable text strings produced by the device.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use and no quick path-specific production evidence for this peripheral field reduce the need for standards reconsideration.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - populated R4 `languageCode` elements are invalid at the R6 path and arbitrary CodeableConcept codings may not satisfy the required language binding.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could retain `languageCode` as CodeableConcept or add `outputLanguage` without deleting the old path. The tradeoff is less uniform language-code validation and extra duplicate fields for a relatively peripheral feature.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a possible Yes alternative, but the practical impact is lower than a Revisit-level concern under FMM 0.

findings.title: specialization and capability were removed and partially replaced by conformsTo and other R6 structures

oldState.summary: R4 had repeatable `specialization` with required `systemType` string and optional `version`, plus repeatable `capability` with required `type` and repeatable `description`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 modeled operating/communication standards in `specialization` and device capabilities in `capability`.

newState.summary: R6 removes those paths and adds repeatable `conformsTo` with required `specification`, optional category/version/source.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `conformsTo` captures standards, specifications, and formal guidance. Capability-like concepts may also need mapping to `property`, `guideline`, or extensions depending on meaning.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `conformsTo` is a strong successor for `specialization` standards but not a complete successor for R4 `capability`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using `specialization` or `capability` contain element paths that do not exist in R6. Mapping `specialization.systemType` strings into R6 CodeableConcept `conformsTo.specification` may require terminology decisions, and R4 capability descriptions have no single obvious R6 home.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 `conformsTo` structure is a reasonable improvement for specifications, standards, versions, and supporting sources. The breakage is material for old paths, but a compatibility design would need to tolerate semantic overlap and uncertain mappings for R4 capability data.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent standards and specifications in a more structured and evidence-friendly way.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `specialization` and `capability` paths while adding `conformsTo` and other structured successors.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 backbones as deprecated aliases or compatibility fields and added `conformsTo` for richer specification data. That would be only partial because R4 `capability` may map to `conformsTo`, `property`, `guideline`, or an extension depending on meaning, and duplicate fields would require profile-specific precedence rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old data but create overlapping conformance and capability concepts, especially because `capability` is not a clean `conformsTo` synonym.

evidence.detail: R4 defines repeatable `specialization` with `systemType` and `version`.
R4 defines repeatable `capability` with `type` and `description`.
R6 defines repeatable `conformsTo` with category, specification, version, and source.

examples.examplesMd: The capability value is intentionally not mapped in the example because the correct R6 target depends on whether it is a standard, static property, operational capability, or implementation-specific extension.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 reorganizes standards and capabilities. The standards portion has a plausible successor in `conformsTo`, but R4 `capability` is not a clean rename. This makes fully automated migration risky.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `specialization` and `capability` are unknown in R6. R6 `conformsTo` data can be only partially reduced to R4 `specialization` because it has category/source and repeatable version details. Capability semantics need human or profile-specific interpretation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map clear standard/specification data to `conformsTo.specification` and `conformsTo.version`. Review `capability` values manually or by profile to decide among `conformsTo`, `property`, `guideline`, or extensions. Test with both standards and non-standard capabilities.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer conformance model is likely justified, but a formal ConceptMap or deprecated aliases would have improved backward compatibility and confidence.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is grouped because R6 appears to split old capability/specialization semantics across more than one area.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4's `specialization` and `capability` captured device communication standards, supported capabilities, and related descriptions. R6's `conformsTo` covers standards/specifications more formally, but it is not a one-for-one replacement for all capability descriptions, and migrating strings or local concepts into formal specification CodeableConcepts can require expert judgment.
keyEvidence: R4 `specialization.systemType` is required when specialization is present and describes the standard used to operate and communicate; `specialization.version` records the version.
R4 `capability.type` and repeatable `capability.description` describe device capabilities.
R6 `conformsTo.specification` is required when conformsTo is present and identifies a standard, specification, protocol, guidance, regulation, legislation, or certification scheme.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens general stability expectations, but this path is close to DeviceDefinition's initial ISO/IEEE 11073 communication-device scope and can affect interoperability/certification meaning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 specialization/capability elements are removed; R6-to-R4 loss and semantic loss are possible because capability descriptions are not fully represented by `conformsTo`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could retain deprecated `specialization` and `capability` while adding `conformsTo`. The tradeoff is overlapping standards/capability representations, but it would avoid lossy expert migration for communication and capability data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the report sees a break and partial alternative, but the Medium impact likely understates the lossiness and centrality of communication/capability data.

findings.title: owner, contact, and onlineInformation support fields were removed or repurposed as publisher metadata

oldState.summary: R4 had owner Reference(Organization), support contact as ContactPoint, and onlineInformation URI.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 administrative/support data was oriented toward the organization responsible for the device and troubleshooting or online device information.

newState.summary: R6 removes owner and onlineInformation; `contact` becomes ContactDetail for the publisher, with new `publisher` string.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 administrative metadata is oriented toward the publisher or steward of the DeviceDefinition rather than support contact for the device itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `owner` and `onlineInformation` are unknown in R6, and R4 `contact` ContactPoint entries are not valid where R6 expects ContactDetail. The semantic shift can also cause support contacts to be misinterpreted as publisher contacts.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning DeviceDefinition with publishable-artifact metadata is reasonable, but removing or repurposing R4 support and owner fields was not clearly necessary. The old fields described device responsibility, troubleshooting, and online information, while R6 publisher/contact describes stewardship of the definition.
justification.inferredGoal: Align DeviceDefinition administrative metadata with publishable artifact conventions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add publisher metadata while retaining explicit owner, support contact, and online information fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backwards-compatible base design could have added `publisher` and publisher contact details while preserving R4 `owner`, support `contact`, and `onlineInformation` under their existing meanings, perhaps with clarified definitions. This would meet the canonical metadata goal and preserve old instances, with the tradeoff of more administrative fields and clearer role guidance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is a larger administrative surface and possible confusion among owner, support, publisher, and steward roles, but those roles are not the same fact.

evidence.detail: R4 defines owner 0..1 Reference(Organization).
R4 contact is 0..* ContactPoint for support/responsible contact.
R4 defines onlineInformation 0..1 uri.
R6 contact is 0..* ContactDetail for publisher communication.
R6 adds publisher 0..1 string.

examples.examplesMd: The example preserves contact details but may change meaning. A support phone number is not necessarily a publisher contact.

findings.narrativeMd: Several R4 device-support fields disappear or change meaning. This is not just a syntactic type change from ContactPoint to ContactDetail; it reflects a shift from device support/ownership to definition publisher/steward metadata.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `owner` and `onlineInformation` fail R6 validation as unknown elements. R4 `contact` entries fail because ContactPoint is not ContactDetail. R6 publisher/contact metadata cannot be represented cleanly in R4 owner/support fields without semantic assumptions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Separate owner, support, publisher, and steward concepts before transforming. ContactPoint values can be wrapped into `ContactDetail.telecom`, but only after deciding whether they are truly publisher contacts. Preserve unmatched owner or support URLs using extensions or related resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 alignment with canonical metadata is understandable, but retaining explicit device owner/support fields would have avoided semantic loss for device catalogs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 distinguished owner/maintenance organization, support contact points, and online information. R6 replaces that surface with publisher/steward metadata and publisher contact details, so old support or maintenance contacts can either be invalid or be migrated into fields with a different accountability meaning.
keyEvidence: R4 `owner` is `Reference(Organization)` for the organization responsible for provision and ongoing maintenance.
R4 `contact` is ContactPoint for support/responsible contacts and comments mention troubleshooting; R4 `onlineInformation` is a URI for online device information.
R6 `publisher` is a string steward name and R6 `contact` is ContactDetail for communicating with the publisher.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Despite FMM 0, support/maintenance contact data is plausibly safety- and business-relevant in device catalog, recall, and troubleshooting workflows, so low maturity does not make the break harmless.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - `owner` and `onlineInformation` are removed and `contact` changes type; semantic/API break - support contacts can be misread as publisher contacts.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could add publisher metadata while retaining explicit owner, support contact, and online-information paths. The tradeoff is overlapping accountability/contact roles, but the roles are distinct enough that preserving them would be cleaner for migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing Yes alternative is well supported; the report's Medium impact may understate the semantic and support-workflow risk.

findings.title: DeviceDefinition.url was repurposed from a device network address to a canonical artifact URL

oldState.summary: R4 `url` was a 0..1 URI network address to contact the device.

semanticText.definition: A network address on which the device may be contacted directly.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 consumers could treat `DeviceDefinition.url` as a device endpoint or online contact address.

newState.summary: R6 `url` is a 0..1 canonical identifier for the DeviceDefinition and is a summary element.

constraints.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

semanticText.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this DeviceDefinition when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 consumers should treat `url` as a stable canonical identifier, not as a device communication endpoint.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The type and cardinality did not change, so many old instances still validate structurally. The break is semantic and runtime-facing: software that dereferences `url` as a device endpoint or uses it for network contact will behave incorrectly under R6 canonical semantics. The new `cnl-1` warning can also surface validation warnings for old URI values containing canonical-problematic characters.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Canonical identity is a strong and reasonable R6 goal, and FHIR canonical-style resources conventionally use `url` for that purpose. The same-name semantic reuse is high risk because old endpoint URLs can still validate, but a fully compatible alternative would weaken interoperability with generic canonical tooling.
justification.inferredGoal: Make DeviceDefinition identifiable by canonical references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 `url` as the device endpoint and add a separate canonical URL element for R6 identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have preserved `DeviceDefinition.url` as the network address and introduced `canonicalUrl` or another explicit identity field. That would protect R4 endpoint semantics, but canonical references and generic canonical processing would need special DeviceDefinition handling instead of using the common `url` pattern.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would avoid semantic breakage but would make DeviceDefinition diverge from generic FHIR canonical-resource conventions where `url` is the canonical identifier.

evidence.detail: R4 definition says `url` is a network address on which the device may be contacted directly.
R6 definition says `url` is the canonical identifier for the DeviceDefinition.
R6 adds a canonical URL warning constraint.

examples.examplesMd: The old example may still be syntactically valid in R6, but it is semantically wrong if it is a live endpoint rather than a persistent canonical identifier.

findings.narrativeMd: `url` is a same-name semantic trap. Automated R4-to-R6 transforms that leave it untouched may produce valid-looking resources with wrong identity semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is usually not an old-valid/new-invalid error because the URI type and 0..1 cardinality remain. The compatibility risk is runtime behavior, canonical resolution, duplicate detection, and search/indexing. Validators may report the R6 `cnl-1` warning for some old values, but the main issue is semantic.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify existing R4 `url` values. If they are device endpoints, move them to an extension, related endpoint inventory, or another implementation-specific location. Populate R6 `url` only with stable canonical identifiers for the DeviceDefinition. Test canonical-reference resolution separately from device connectivity.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new element would have been less disruptive, but FHIR canonical resources conventionally use `url`. The change is probably justified for consistency, yet it requires explicit migration review because validation alone will not catch all misuse.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The same `url` element changes from a device network address in R4 to the canonical identifier for the DeviceDefinition in R6. This can be worse than a validation break: an R4 endpoint URI may still validate as a URI in R6 but be used as a stable canonical artifact identifier, changing lookup, reference, caching, and publication behavior.
keyEvidence: R4 `DeviceDefinition.url` is a network address on which the device may be contacted directly; if the device runs a FHIR server, the comment says it should be the base URL.
R6 `DeviceDefinition.url` is an absolute URI canonical identifier used when referenced in a specification, model, design, or instance and remains the same across servers.
R6 adds canonical warning constraint `cnl-1` for characters that complicate canonical reference processing.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 reduces general stability expectations, but a same-path semantic flip between endpoint and canonical identity is a high-risk migration trap independent of maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen - instances may pass structural validation while systems interpret an endpoint URI as a canonical artifact URL; warning-level - some old endpoint strings can trigger the new canonical URL warning.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could preserve R4 `url` as a device endpoint and add a distinct canonical identifier, or add an endpoint field before deprecating the old use. The tradeoff is inconsistency with FHIR's common canonical-resource `url` pattern, but the current same-name repurposing is especially risky.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high-risk assessment and partial alternative are supported, even though the break is primarily semantic/runtime rather than old-valid/new-invalid.

findings.title: parentDevice, quantity, and physicalCharacteristics were removed while R6 adds different relationship and packaging structures

oldState.summary: R4 had direct parent device reference, package/device quantity, and ProdCharacteristic physical characteristics.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 directly recorded the parent device it can be part of, a quantity in packaging, and a typed ProdCharacteristic for dimensions or similar traits.

newState.summary: R6 removes those direct paths and adds `hasPart`, recursive `packaging`, and broader `property` semantics.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express parts, packaging, and static characteristics, but not as direct one-for-one replacements for the R4 fields.

facts.newValue: R6 structures are not direct one-for-one successors.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `hasPart` is directionally related to `parentDevice` but is inverse-like rather than the same path; `packaging.count` is related to R4 `quantity` but has integer packaging semantics; `property` may carry static characteristics but lacks the old ProdCharacteristic shape.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using any of these direct fields are invalid in R6. Mapping requires structural and sometimes directional changes, especially for parent/part relationships and quantity versus packaging count.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 structures appear to support richer modeling of parts, packaging, and static characteristics, but the supplied computable definitions do not establish a complete rationale or one-to-one mapping for the removed R4 fields. The goal is plausible, while the necessity of this amount of breakage remains uncertain.
justification.inferredGoal: Provide richer R6 modeling for parts, packaging, and static characteristics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain legacy parent, quantity, and physical-characteristic fields while adding richer `hasPart`, `packaging`, and property structures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `parentDevice`, `quantity`, and `physicalCharacteristics` as deprecated compatibility fields while adding the richer R6 structures. That alternative is only partial because `parentDevice` and `hasPart` can express opposite graph directions, `quantity` as Quantity is not the same as integer package count, and physical traits could be duplicated between `ProdCharacteristic` and `property`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility aliases would reduce data loss but create overlapping relationship directions, package-count semantics, and physical-characteristic representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines parentDevice 0..1 Reference(DeviceDefinition).
R4 defines quantity 0..1 Quantity for packaging quantity.
R4 defines physicalCharacteristics 0..1 ProdCharacteristic.
R6 adds repeatable hasPart with required definition[x] and optional count.
R6 adds recursive packaging with count, distributor, UDI, and nested packaging.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 `parentDevice` example has no simple same-resource R6 equivalent. A migration may need to update the parent resource to use `hasPart`, or use `link` or an extension depending on intended semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 remodels physical composition and packaging rather than preserving the R4 direct fields. This creates old-to-new validation breaks and nontrivial graph transforms.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `parentDevice`, `quantity`, and `physicalCharacteristics` are unknown R6 elements. R6 `hasPart` and recursive `packaging` content cannot be flattened cleanly into R4. Some R4 quantities may map to integer `packaging.count`, but unit-bearing or non-integer quantities do not.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat these fields as manual or rule-driven migrations. For parent relationships, decide whether to invert links onto parent resources, use R6 `hasPart`, or preserve source semantics in an extension. For packaging quantities, map only clear integer package counts to `packaging.count`; preserve units or complex physical traits separately.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 structures are richer, but direct aliases for old fields would have reduced data loss. Without official mapping notes, conservative migration should preserve original R4 values when a clean target is not obvious.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had direct fields for parent device, packaging quantity, and physical characteristics. R6 uses different structures: child-oriented `hasPart`, recursive `packaging`, and more general `property`. That is not a local rename; parent relationships may require updating a different resource, Quantity packaging data can be narrowed to integer counts, and physical characteristics need coded property modeling.
keyEvidence: R4 `parentDevice` is 0..1 `Reference(DeviceDefinition)`, `quantity` is 0..1 Quantity for package contents, and `physicalCharacteristics` is 0..1 ProdCharacteristic.
R6 `hasPart.definition[x]` is required when `hasPart` is present, `packaging.count` is integer, and `property` is a general static-characteristic backbone.
R4 DeviceDefinition scope says the resource supports catalog definitions and hierarchical device configurations.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 softens broad stability concerns, but hierarchy, packaging, and physical characteristics are central to device catalog and regulatory/UDI-style data, and migration can be non-local or lossy.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - the R4 direct elements are removed; R6-to-R4 loss/semantic loss - the new structures are not one-for-one replacements for parent, Quantity, and ProdCharacteristic data.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could retain deprecated `parentDevice`, `quantity`, and `physicalCharacteristics` while adding richer `hasPart`, `packaging`, and `property` structures. The tradeoff is duplicate hierarchy/packaging representations, but it would avoid non-local inversion and lossy quantity/characteristic mapping.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the report correctly identifies only a partial alternative, but Medium impact likely understates the non-local and lossy migration burden.

findings.title: R6 adds many optional DeviceDefinition-specific backbones with no R4 base representation

affectedLocation.newPath: DeviceDefinition.regulatoryIdentifier, DeviceDefinition.deviceVersion, DeviceDefinition.link, DeviceDefinition.guideline, DeviceDefinition.correctiveAction, DeviceDefinition.chargeItem

oldState.summary: R4 has no local elements for the listed R6 regulatory, version, linkage, usage, corrective-action, or billing details.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can only preserve these concepts through extensions, related resources, or out-of-band data.

newState.summary: R6 adds several optional but structured DeviceDefinition areas, many with mandatory children when the optional parent is present.
newState.narrativeMd: Examples include `regulatoryIdentifier`, UDI market distribution details, `hasPart`, `packaging`, `deviceVersion`, `link`, `productionIdentifierInUDI`, `guideline`, `correctiveAction`, and `chargeItem`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These additions do not make old R4 instances invalid by themselves because the parent elements are optional. They do create substantial R6-to-R4 representability risk and generated-model drift: R6 instances can carry regulatory identifiers, corrective action, billing, and guideline data that R4 has no base fields for.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added regulatory, version, linkage, guideline, corrective-action, and charge-item structures serve new R6 information needs and are optional. They create substantial R6-to-R4 representability risk, but they are not an R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.inferredGoal: Expand DeviceDefinition coverage for regulatory, packaging, lifecycle, clinical-use, relationship, and billing use cases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are optional additive R6 elements and do not make R4 instances invalid in R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the issue is optional R6 expressiveness rather than old R4 content becoming invalid, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Avoiding the new fields would preserve R4 round trips but would fail the R6 goal of representing these additional domains; cross-version extensions are mitigation for down-conversion, not a backwards-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions or mappings may be needed, but those are converter mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 differential adds new local elements including regulatoryIdentifier, hasPart, packaging, deviceVersion, link, guideline, correctiveAction, and chargeItem.
No corresponding R4 local elements exist for these R6-only structures.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses R6-only regulatory and corrective-action content. R4 has no base fields for these structures.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 substantially expands the resource. This is not an old-data validation break, but it is one of the largest bidirectional migration issues for DeviceDefinition because R6 data can be much richer than R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators reject these R6-only fields. Converters that drop them lose regulatory, safety, billing, or use-guidance content. Generated R6 models will also contain many properties absent from R4 models.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, define cross-version extensions or companion resources for each populated R6-only area. Do not silently drop corrective-action, regulatory, or charge-item data. For R4-to-R6, leave optional additions absent unless source data or business rules can populate them.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are mostly justified and optional. The backward-compatible concern is less about the R6 design and more about needing official extension and mapping guidance for systems that must round-trip to R4.

freshReview.narrativeMd: These are optional R6 additions. They can be important for R6-to-R4 downgrade scenarios, especially regulatory identifiers, corrective actions, and billing links, but they do not make any R4 DeviceDefinition instance invalid in R6. Adding optional structures is normal standards evolution rather than a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design problem.
keyEvidence: R6 adds optional structures including `regulatoryIdentifier`, `deviceVersion`, `link`, `guideline`, `correctiveAction`, and `chargeItem`; required children apply only when an optional parent is present.
R4 lacks direct base elements for several of these R6 structures.
ONC ISP lists UDI representation specifications as Final/Production, confirming some new regulatory data can be important, but the change is additive for R4-to-R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 further reduces concern because the finding is not a forward compatibility break; regulatory importance affects downgrade planning, not whether R6 should add optional fields.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss - populated R6-only fields may not round-trip to R4 without extensions, but old R4 instances are not rejected by R6 because of these additions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for optional additive fields. R4 downgrade support belongs in extensions, profiles, or conversion guidance rather than blocking the R6 model from adding structured content.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing High impact overstates a reverse-direction representability issue as a breaking compatibility concern.

findings.title: Many local elements became summary elements in R6

oldState.summary: R4 local DeviceDefinition elements were mostly not marked isSummary, aside from some inherited/backbone modifierExtension elements and `safety`/`parentDevice`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `_summary` behavior for local DeviceDefinition data was comparatively sparse.

newState.summary: R6 marks many local metadata and classification/name elements as summary.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 summary flags appear on `url`, `identifier`, `version`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `name`, `title`, `status`, `experimental`, `date`, `publisher`, `contact`, `useContext`, `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, `manufacturer`, `modelNumber`, `deviceName`, `classification`, `conformsTo`, and `hasPart`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flags do not affect instance validity, but they can change `_summary=true`, generated summary views, indexing decisions, and code that assumes summary payloads are small or stable.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Expanding the summary surface is plausible for a catalog-like R6 DeviceDefinition because identifiers, names, status, classification, and conformance metadata are useful for discovery. The change can affect clients and payload sizes, but it does not make old R4 instances invalid.
justification.inferredGoal: Expose key canonical and catalog fields in summary responses.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: summary flag changes affect runtime summary behavior, not R4 instance validity against the R6 base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Since this finding is runtime-only, the compact alternative judgment is `Not applicable`. R6 could have changed summary flags more conservatively, but that is an operational compatibility choice rather than a less-breaking design needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping R4 summary flags would reduce `_summary` churn but is not a backwards-compatible alternative to an instance-breaking base design.

evidence.detail: R4 local elements such as identifier, deviceName, modelNumber, and contact are not marked summary.
R6 marks numerous local elements as summary, including url, identifier, version, status, manufacturer, deviceName, classification, conformsTo, and hasPart.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed because summary flags affect server response shaping and generated metadata rather than JSON validity.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes the summary surface for DeviceDefinition. Clients using `_summary`, summary serialization, or summary-field-based indexing may see more and different fields.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an R4-valid/R6-invalid change. The risk is runtime behavior: summary responses, code generation metadata, and indexing pipelines may include or omit different local fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review clients and tests that use `_summary=true`, summary element lists, generated model annotations, or summary-based search/index payloads. Update expected fields and payload-size assumptions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is likely justified by the R6 catalog model. Maintaining R4 summary flags would reduce runtime churn but make R6 summaries less useful.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The summary-flag changes affect metadata about what may appear in summary responses or generated model annotations; they do not invalidate R4 content or remove data. Clients may see more fields in R6 summary views, but summary responses are already intentionally partial and version-specific.
keyEvidence: R4 marks only a small set of local/backbone DeviceDefinition elements as summary, including `safety` and `parentDevice` plus inherited/modifierExtension paths.
R6 marks many metadata, identity, classification, manufacturer, and relationship elements as summary.
The finding changes `isSummary` metadata only, not cardinality, type, binding, or element presence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use and the metadata-only nature of the finding both soften compatibility concern; no path-specific production evidence indicates summary flags are a critical migration blocker.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling - `_summary` behavior and generated metadata may change, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could leave summary flags unchanged, but marking definitional identity/classification fields as summary is a reasonable metadata choice and preserving old flags would not materially improve instance compatibility.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing Medium runtime impact is too strong for a metadata-only summary change on a low-FMM resource.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are stable. The StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active, which is noted as non-breaking metadata.
No local error-level invariants specific to DeviceDefinition were added or removed. R6 adds the `cnl-1` warning on `url`, covered in the URL semantic finding.
No local non-extension DeviceDefinition element became a modifier or ceased to be a modifier. Backbone `modifierExtension` behavior is inherited/base infrastructure and excluded from findings.
No material local slicing changes were identified in the DeviceDefinition snapshot/differential comparison.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were identified as materially changed.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were identified beyond the `cnl-1` URL warning constraint already reported.
Existing Organization and DeviceDefinition reference target changes are covered where local paths changed. No additional target-profile narrowing was found for unchanged local reference paths.
Major removals, additions, and likely replacements were assessed. Stable local areas include the core UDI-DI child fields, `safety`, `shelfLifeStorage`, `note`, and material boolean flags.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This changes metadata about the definition, not the instance shape of `DeviceDefinition`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Consumers that filter artifacts by maturity/status may treat the R6 resource differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: UDI-DI core fields are stable but R6 adds deviceIdentifierSystem and marketDistribution
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The existing R4 required UDI-DI children `deviceIdentifier`, `issuer`, and `jurisdiction` retain their cardinalities and primitive URI/string types.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 can represent additional UDI namespace and market availability details that R4 cannot represent directly.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: material.substance gains an example binding and richer explanatory text
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains 1..1 CodeableConcept under the optional `material` backbone, and the new binding is example strength.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migration can preserve R4 material codes, but implementations may want to align with the R6 substance-code example value set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds many optional canonical metadata elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Optional additions such as `name`, `title`, `experimental`, `date`, `useContext`, and `jurisdiction` do not make old R4 instances invalid by themselves.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: They support richer R6 cataloging but increase R6-to-R4 data loss unless preserved through extensions.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited `DomainResource`, `Resource`, `Element`, and extension behavior was intentionally excluded by scope. Base-artifact reports should own any inherited class-hierarchy or infrastructure changes.
R4-to-R6 migration needs a reviewed mapping from removed R4 device name type codes to R6 `registered-name`, retained codes, local codings, or extensions.
Device classification migration depends on terminology expansion and policy for mapping R4 `device-kind` concepts into R6 `device-type` and repeatable `classification`.
The R6 package contains a different and expanded DeviceDefinition search surface. This report is scoped to the resource StructureDefinition, so search behavior should be assessed separately.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 DeviceDefinition diff, ballot change note, or Jira rationale was used. Semantic matches were inferred from StructureDefinition paths, definitions, and local terminology.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use the official HL7 diff/change log and committee notes for DeviceDefinition.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology analysis used local ValueSet/CodeSystem JSON. SNOMED-backed and all-languages expansions were not evaluated through a terminology server.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for both package versions and compare expanded concepts with official versioned terminology dependencies.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMaps were available for renamed/split fields or device-nametype code migration, so several migration recommendations require human policy decisions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official cross-version maps or produce project-approved ConceptMaps and extension policies.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build. Element names, cardinalities, bindings, or definitions could change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final published R6 core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Expected prevalence was estimated from model structure only. No production corpus of R4 DeviceDefinition instances was analyzed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Profile a representative R4 instance corpus and count populated paths.
